column1: # Negentropy's counted refinement columns — the external anchor for `benches/protocol.rs` (#362).
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Every other comparison `benches/protocol.rs` supports is reconcile-rs
# against reconcile-rs: policy against policy, `b` against `b`. This fixture is the one column
# produced by a *different implementation of the same algorithm family*, so the harness can print a
# figure that is not self-referential.
# PROVENANCE — regenerating this file is a manual, out-of-band act, by design (#362 "Accepted cost,
# named up front"; same posture as `img/perf-*.png`). It is NOT reproducible by a plain
# `cargo bench`, and nothing in CI reads it.
#   implementation:  https://github.com/hoytech/negentropy  (the reference implementation, the one
#                    arXiv:2603.19820's own evaluation cites)
#   driver:          benches/fixtures/negentropy-drive.js  (committed beside this file)
#   command:         cp benches/fixtures/negentropy-drive.js <negentropy>/js/drive.js
#                    cd <negentropy>/js && node --max-old-space-size=4096 drive.js <n> <d>
#   generated:       2026-08-20, node v22.22.2
# HOW THE COUNTS ARE OBTAINED. The driver does not read Negentropy's internals. It parses the
# emitted wire messages against the published grammar in Negentropy's own protocol v1 spec
# (docs/negentropy-protocol-v1.md, in the upstream repository named above):
#   Message := <protocolVersion (Byte)> <Range>*
#   Range   := <upperBound (Bound)> <mode (Varint)> <payload (Skip | Fingerprint | IdList)>
#   Bound   := <encodedTimestamp (Varint)> <length (Varint)> <idPrefix (Byte)*>
# so it doubles as a conformance check on our reading of that spec: the parser asserts it consumes
# every message to the byte, and would fail loudly if the grammar and the implementation disagreed.
# COMMENSURABILITY — READ BEFORE SUMMING ANYTHING AGAINST OUR OWN TOTALS (#362 non-goals).
#  1. ONLY THE REFINEMENT COLUMNS COMPARE. `fp_ranges`/`fp_bytes` below count mode=1
#     (Fingerprint) ranges only, which is what `Cost::ranges`/`Cost::refinement_bytes` count on our
#     side. The `idlist_*` columns are recorded for completeness and are NOT commensurable with our
#     IDLIST columns: a Negentropy element is a 64-bit timestamp + a 256-bit id, ours is a key + an
#     HLC + a *value* of arbitrary size. Do not add the two totals together.
#  2. THE INSTANCE IS MODELLED, NOT SHARED. Our store is keyed by `u64` and ordered by key;
#     Negentropy orders by (timestamp, id). The driver gives item `k` timestamp `k` and a
#     deterministic 32-byte id, so both implementations refine over the same logical ordering of the
#     same `n` items with the same `d` spread evenly — `Clustering::Spread`. It is the same
#     *instance shape*, not the same bytes.
#  3. SAME FAN-OUT, DIFFERENT DESCENT. Both run `b = 16`. They still do not advertise the same
#     number of ranges (see `benches/README.md`); that difference is a finding, not an error bar.
# COLUMNS. `fp_bytes` is the on-wire cost of the mode=1 ranges *including* each range's bound and
# mode varint, not the 16-byte fingerprint payload alone — the whole point of the anchor is that a
# per-range figure must price the framing the range cannot travel without.
